anti_overlap: Do not evaluate the correctness of the sanitize_untrusted.py implementation — fd-safety covers security boundary correctness
Do not assess roadmap dependency sequencing for schedule purposes — fd-broadcast-scheduling covers slot ordering
Do not evaluate whether agent spec validation logic is architecturally correct — fd-architecture covers that
decision_lens: A defect found in production costs 10x a defect found in test. A test suite that does not exist costs more than a test suite that exists but is incomplete. Evaluate the roadmap's test scaffolding posture: does the sequencing of new features ahead of test infrastructure mean that defects accumulate faster than measurement capacity? Flag any workstream that adds new behavior to untested code without a paired test plan.
distance_rationale: Kaizen event quality engineering operates on production lines with zero automated inspection, sequencing defect-cluster fixes by root cause and measurement infrastructure — the same challenge as a 5,500-LOC untested codebase where new workstreams outpace test coverage, but in a factory floor context rather than software.
expected_isomorphisms: Defect found in production vs. in test cost ratio maps to bugs found by user vs. by unit test. 'Measurement system before claiming improvement' maps to 'CI gate before claiming B5 shell hygiene is durable'. Root-cause clustering maps to tracing multiple P0 findings to the same integration boundary gap.
focus: Test coverage gaps, defect-cluster patterns, and incremental quality improvement sequencing in a 5,500-LOC untested codebase
name: fd-kaizen-testability
persona: Apply the perspective of a manufacturing quality engineer running a kaizen event on a production line with zero automated inspection — one who must identify the highest-leverage defect clusters, sequence corrective actions by root cause rather than symptom, and establish measurement systems before claiming improvement.
review_areas: Assess the '0 unit tests in 5,500 LOC' finding: the roadmap lists test scaffolding as P3/Later while C1 (lib_registry.py), C2 (dispatch state machine), and C3 (sanitize_untrusted fuzz tests) are P2/Later — verify that this sequencing does not mean new behavior ships before the test infrastructure to catch regressions exists

Check whether the blueprint workstreams (B5 shell hygiene, B6 phase-file accuracy, C1–C4) have explicit test plans or test-file targets listed; workstreams without named test artifacts are process steps with no inspection checkpoint

Identify defect clusters from the roadmap's 'What's Not Working' section: 4 P0 Track B6 findings + bead/code drift + research-mode parity gap — are these independent defects or do they share a common root cause (e.g. lack of contract enforcement at integration boundaries) that should be fixed once upstream?

Verify that the C3 workstream (sanitize_untrusted.py fuzz tests + TrustedContent NewType) is correctly sequenced after B3 (shipped) rather than being deferred to Later while B3's security guarantees are exercised in production without fuzz validation

Check that the FluxBench closed-loop scoring (shipped) has its own regression protection — if fluxbench-score.sh changes break scoring silently, the drift detection mechanism itself becomes unreliable
Assess whether the validate_agent_spec() function (B2, shipped) has unit tests; the anti_overlap incident (116 corrupted files) was fixed by B2, but without tests, the same boundary can regress

severity_examples.condition: When C2 remains unscheduled and no intermediate test checkpoint is defined for the existing dispatch path
severity_examples.scenario: C2 (dispatch state machine, 8-12h, design-intensive) is scheduled as Later/P3 while the dispatch path it formalizes is exercised by every flux-drive run — new features built on an untested state machine accumulate hidden regression surface

severity_examples.condition: When test_validate_agent_spec.py is listed as Later/P3 and no bead guards against validate_agent_spec() regressions
severity_examples.scenario: validate_agent_spec() (the fix for the 116-file corruption incident) has no unit test — a future refactor can silently re-open the boundary gap

severity_examples.condition: When B5 does not include adding shellcheck to the CI pipeline as part of its acceptance criteria
severity_examples.scenario: B5 (shell hygiene, 3h, independent) is listed as P2 without a shellcheck CI gate — shell hygiene work without a CI check is a one-time cleanup with no defect prevention mechanism

success_hints: For each new workstream that adds behavior (C1, C2, C4), state which test file would catch a regression — if none exists, flag as a missing inspection checkpoint
Distinguish between 'test scaffolding' (infrastructure) and 'test cases' (coverage) — the roadmap needs both, and sequencing infrastructure first is the correct order
When identifying defect clusters, trace to the integration boundary (LLM-JSON → render_agent, dispatch → resolver, sanitize boundary) rather than the symptom — root-cause fixes prevent whole clusters
task_context: interflux has ~5,500 LOC of shell + Python with zero unit tests. The roadmap defers test scaffolding to P3 while shipping new behavioral workstreams at P2. Review through the lens of kaizen-event defect triage: identify the highest-leverage test gaps, assess sequencing correctness, and flag cases where new behavior is added without paired inspection.
